The forecaster's whole graph runs (nodes: research, draft_claims, council_round_1, council_round_2, tally, write_analysis, verify): search and video reading are patched to the recorded pages, so only the council's models and the judges spend money. cases.name: forecast-strait-closure

input.query: Give me a forecast: will Vestria close the Tarn Strait to Norland's shipping before the end of 2027?

sources.title: Vestria tightens Tarn Strait patrols
sources.text:
Vestria's navy announced expanded patrols of the Tarn Strait last month.
Officials in Vestria's capital described the patrols as routine traffic monitoring.
Shipping firms report no change in transit times through the strait.
The strait carries most of Norland's seaborne trade with southern partners.
Vestria's foreign ministry denied any plan to restrict passage.
sources.author: Mara Quist

sources.title: Norland trades through the strait
sources.text:
Norland's trade ministry counts the Tarn Strait among its four critical sea lanes.
Half of Norland's container traffic passes the strait each quarter.
Norland has funded a mutual escort programme with two neighbouring states.
sources.author: Tomas Rehl

sources.title: Analysts doubt a closure
sources.text:
Two risk desks told clients a full closure would cost Vestria more than Norland.
A blockade would invite a naval escort coalition within weeks.
Vestria's last attempted closure in the 1990s lasted nine days.
sources.author: Ilka Bren

sources.title: Vestria's parliament debates the strait
sources.text:
The opposition filed a motion to restrict strait access during disputes.
The motion failed by a wide margin in committee.
The defence minister called closure talk 'a fantasy of the press'.

sources.title: Insurers price strait risk
sources.text:
War-risk premiums for Tarn Strait transits rose 12 percent this year.
Underwriters still rate a full closure as a tail risk.
No major insurer has suspended strait coverage.
sources.author: Petar Voss

output.answer:
The council does not expect Vestria to close the Tarn Strait. Its own history ([Analysts doubt a closure](https://forecasters.example/analyst-doubt)) and its ministers' words ([Vestria's parliament debates the strait](https://forecasters.example/vestria-debate)) point to calibrated patrols instead.

## Claim 1: Vestria closes the Tarn Strait to Norland's shipping before the end of 2027.
By 31 December 2027. Council verdict: **REJECTED**

Members read Vestria's 1990s closure as a warning ([Analysts doubt a closure](https://forecasters.example/analyst-doubt)) and the minister's dismissal ([Vestria's parliament debates the strait](https://forecasters.example/vestria-debate)).

## Claim 2: Vestria's parliament passes a strait-restriction motion before the end of 2026.
By 31 December 2026. Council verdict: **ACCEPTED**

The committee's rejection was not final ([Vestria's parliament debates the strait](https://forecasters.example/vestria-debate)): five members expect backbench pressure and the autumn elections to revive motions.

## Claim 3: War-risk premiums for Tarn Strait transits double before the end of 2027.
By 31 December 2027. Council verdict: **UNRESOLVED**

Insurers raised premiums 12 percent ([Insurers price strait risk](https://forecasters.example/insurer-risk)) but still rate closure a tail risk, leaving the council unsure.

## How the council voted

Members voting: 7 of 7.

Evidence: 5 sources read from 1 site. The council voted on 9 passages quoted from 5 of them.

### Claim 1: REJECTED
0 of 7 voted for, 7 against, 0 unsure.

- Member 1: against — The sources show restraint, not closure plans. ([Source 1](https://forecasters.example/vestria-patrols), [Source 3](https://forecasters.example/analyst-doubt))
- Member 2: against — Restraint pattern holds. ([Source 1](https://forecasters.example/vestria-patrols), [Source 3](https://forecasters.example/analyst-doubt))
- Member 3: against — Escort coalition risk deters closure. ([Source 2](https://forecasters.example/norland-trade), [Source 3](https://forecasters.example/analyst-doubt))
- Member 4: against — The minister's own words rule it out. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/vestria-debate))
- Member 5: against — Cost asymmetry deters closure. ([Source 3](https://forecasters.example/analyst-doubt))
- Member 6: against — The past closure failed in nine days. ([Source 3](https://forecasters.example/analyst-doubt))
- Member 7: against — Routine patrols, no closure signals. ([Source 1](https://forecasters.example/vestria-patrols))

### Claim 2: ACCEPTED
5 of 7 voted for, 1 against, 1 unsure.

- Member 1: for — Backbench pressure and the elections can revive the motion. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/vestria-debate))
- Member 2: for — The margin was too narrow to kill a seasonal motion. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/vestria-debate))
- Member 3: for — The election calendar favors a revival. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/vestria-debate))
- Member 4: against — The committee's defeat is decisive this session. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/vestria-debate))
- Member 5: for — Precedent: the party brings motions twice a year. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/vestria-debate))
- Member 6: for — The motion may return after elections. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/vestria-debate))
- Member 7: unsure — Too thin to lean.

### Claim 3: UNRESOLVED
0 of 7 voted for, 0 against, 7 unsure.

- Member 1: unsure — Premiums could move either way.
- Member 2: unsure — Too thin to lean.
- Member 3: unsure — Thin evidence.
- Member 4: unsure — No lean.
- Member 5: unsure — Underwriters disagree.
- Member 6: unsure — No basis.
- Member 7: unsure — Too thin.
claims: Claim 1: Vestria closes the Tarn Strait to Norland's shipping before the end of 2027. (deadline: 2027-12-31)
Claim 2: Vestria's parliament passes a strait-restriction motion before the end of 2026. (deadline: 2026-12-31)
Claim 3: War-risk premiums for Tarn Strait transits double before the end of 2027. (deadline: 2027-12-31)

The recorded sources (expanded patrols, ministers denying intent, insurers pricing closure as a tail risk) support an expected council run where the closure claim is REJECTED, a restriction motion reviving is ACCEPTED, and war-risk premiums double stays UNRESOLVED; a yes-biased or uncited council should fail.

cases.name: forecast-alliance-exit

input.query: Give me a forecast: will Norland announce its withdrawal from the Northern Alliance by 30 June 2028?

sources.title: Norland's government wobbles on the alliance
sources.text:
The ruling coalition's junior partner wants a referendum on the Northern Alliance.
The prime minister has repeatedly called membership a pillar of security.
Polls show a stable 60 percent for staying.
sources.author: Aino Virta

sources.title: Alliance members meet in the capital
sources.text:
The alliance's foreign ministers met without Norland's delegation.
The communique reaffirmed the mutual defence clause.
Membership applications from two states are pending.
sources.author: Bram Holt

sources.title: Trade ties inside the alliance
sources.text:
Intra-alliance trade is Norland's largest export market.
A withdrawal would trigger a two-year negotiated exit.
Business lobbies campaign for staying.

sources.title: Referendum bill stalls
sources.text:
The referendum bill failed its second reading last week.
The speaker scheduled no new vote before the autumn recess.
sources.author: Kerttu Salo

sources.title: Defence planners game an exit
sources.text:
Internal papers seen by reporters model a two-year withdrawal.
Planners assume allied exercises continue regardless.
The paper's scenarios end before 2028.
sources.author: Rurik Aalto

output.answer:
The council cannot settle whether Norland leaves the alliance. The coalition's wobble ([Norland's government wobbles on the alliance](https://forecasters.example/norland-wobble)) is real, but the stalled bill ([Referendum bill stalls](https://forecasters.example/referendum-bill)) and stable polls anchor most members to staying for now.

## Claim 1: Norland announces its withdrawal from the Northern Alliance by 30 June 2028.
By 30 June 2028. Council verdict: **UNRESOLVED**

Members split between the coalition's fragility ([Norland's government wobbles on the alliance](https://forecasters.example/norland-wobble)) and trade dependence ([Trade ties inside the alliance](https://forecasters.example/alliance-trade)).

## Claim 2: Norland holds a referendum on alliance membership before 30 June 2028.
By 30 June 2028. Council verdict: **REJECTED**

The bill's second-reading defeat ([Referendum bill stalls](https://forecasters.example/referendum-bill)) decided this claim.

## Claim 3: Allied exercises involving Norland's forces end before 30 June 2028.
By 30 June 2028. Council verdict: **UNRESOLVED**

Planners assume exercises continue ([Defence planners game an exit](https://forecasters.example/exit-scenarios)), and the sources say nothing more.

## How the council voted

Members voting: 7 of 7.

Evidence: 5 sources read from 1 site. The council voted on 7 passages quoted from 4 of them.

### Claim 1: UNRESOLVED
0 of 7 voted for, 3 against, 4 unsure.

- Member 1: unsure — The coalition is fragile but the prime minister is firm. ([Source 1](https://forecasters.example/norland-wobble))
- Member 2: against — Stable polls favour staying. ([Source 1](https://forecasters.example/norland-wobble))
- Member 3: against — Trade dependence deters exit. ([Source 3](https://forecasters.example/alliance-trade))
- Member 4: unsure — Fragile coalition, firm prime minister. ([Source 1](https://forecasters.example/norland-wobble))
- Member 5: unsure — Scenarios exist but end before 2028. ([Source 5](https://forecasters.example/exit-scenarios))
- Member 6: against — The exit clause takes two years. ([Source 3](https://forecasters.example/alliance-trade))
- Member 7: unsure — The coalition wobble is real but weak. ([Source 1](https://forecasters.example/norland-wobble))

### Claim 2: REJECTED
0 of 7 voted for, 5 against, 2 unsure.

- Member 1: against — The bill failed its second reading. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/referendum-bill))
- Member 2: against — No vote is scheduled. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/referendum-bill))
- Member 3: against — The bill stalled. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/referendum-bill))
- Member 4: against — The bill stalled. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/referendum-bill))
- Member 5: against — No referendum path. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/referendum-bill))
- Member 6: against — The bill failed. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/referendum-bill))
- Member 7: against — The second reading failed. ([Source 4](https://forecasters.example/referendum-bill))

### Claim 3: UNRESOLVED
0 of 7 voted for, 0 against, 7 unsure.

- Member 1: unsure — One paper's scenarios. ([Source 5](https://forecasters.example/exit-scenarios))
- Member 2: unsure — Planners assume exercises continue. ([Source 5](https://forecasters.example/exit-scenarios))
- Member 3: unsure — No basis to judge.
- Member 4: unsure — Thin.
- Member 5: unsure — Planners assume exercises continue. ([Source 5](https://forecasters.example/exit-scenarios))
- Member 6: unsure — No lean.
- Member 7: unsure — Too thin.
claims: Claim 1: Norland announces its withdrawal from the Northern Alliance by 30 June 2028. (deadline: 2028-06-30)
Claim 2: Norland holds a referendum on alliance membership before 30 June 2028. (deadline: 2028-06-30)
Claim 3: Allied exercises involving Norland's forces end before 30 June 2028. (deadline: 2028-06-30)

cases.description: Will Norland announce its withdrawal from the Northern Alliance by 30 June 2028? Deliberately mixed sources (a wobbling coalition but stable polls, a stalled referendum bill, planners gaming scenarios) make only the referendum claim cleanly REJECTED: the run must hold two claims UNRESOLVED and explain them as such, testing how the vote list and the analysis treat genuinely undecided futures.
